deep_patterns: integration, not addition, is the non-arbitrary measure of good design — named twice, in engineering and in philosophy
why: Fuller's synergy (whole-system behavior no single part predicts — the dome holds loads no single strut could, because the behavior lives in the coupling) is structurally identical to Simondon's concretization (a design becomes more itself as separate functions converge into one resonant whole). Same claim about what makes a design genuinely good, arrived at independently from engineering and from philosophy of technology.
evidence: Simondon: "A concrete one is integrated: a single feature serves several functions at once, parts resonate with and cool and brace each other" (Simondon.md:54). Fuller: "synergy (whole-system behavior unpredicted by the parts — the dome holds loads no single strut could, because the behavior lives in the coupling, not the components)" (People/Buckminster Fuller.md:66).
